A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-steering study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-following experiments with Phi-3, Gemma 2, and Mistral, including response-quality evaluation, multiple-instruction steering, and transfer to base models.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds exact-length experiments, parameter-selection diagnostics, representation visualizations, and accuracy–quality trade-off analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds a GPT-2 perplexity screen to layer/weight selection, rejecting configurations that produce excessively low-perplexity outputs before maximizing validation accuracy (Appendix E). This refines the selection procedure; contrastive vector construction, scaling equations, and additive/subtractive steering remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation requiring exactly 1–5 sentences (Appendix J, Figure 17b–c), extending v1's maximum-length constraints and general conciseness/verbosity tasks. The underlying IFEval coverage, languages, and other instruction families are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 19 adds an explicit accuracy/perplexity comparison between adding word-exclusion vectors and subtracting word-inclusion vectors. v1 discusses the former's problematic token projections in Section 5 but does not report this comparative evaluation. Existing standard-inference and same-model-steering comparators remain.

E3.justification: The reported word-validation protocol changes from a small manually created prompt set to 276 GPT-4o-generated question–word pairs. v2 introduces quality-constrained parameter selection, revises selected layers in Tables 8–9, and changes the keyword-generation limit from 2048 to 1024 tokens while retaining 2048 for format/length experiments. These materially alter experimental settings; additional exact-length and sensitivity experiments introduce further evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: t-SNE analyses of instruction vectors, per-instruction accuracy and quality breakdowns across models, layer/weight selection diagnostics, a word-exclusion accuracy–quality sweep, and comparison of exclusion-vector strategies (Figures 11–19). v1's cosine-similarity analyses, failure examples, and verbosity sweep are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions use exact McNemar tests with the same significance threshold, three GPT-4o quality-evaluation runs with means and standard errors, and paired two-sided t-tests for quality-score distributions. Changed p-values and significance markers are result changes, not changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Several principal results change: Figure 6a loses the significance markers for word inclusion without instructions, and Figure 8a reverses the cross-model versus same-model ranking for Gemma 2 9B. Figure 10b's mean quality delta changes from -0.05 to approximately zero. v2 also adds exact-length and extensive diagnostic results. Revised settings prevent interpreting these collectively as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and steering equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added empirical diagnostics do not introduce new theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about controlling format, length, keywords, and simultaneous instructions remain. The introduction and conclusion narrow cross-model superiority from a general or 'often' claim to 'can sometimes' and 'in some cases,' consistent with the revised comparison.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands limitations, including untested example-count sensitivity, imperfect instruction representations, the inability of perplexity screening to catch factual/logical errors, and transfer restricted to matching model families and sizes. New analyses interpret steering-strength trade-offs and representation geometry. Section 7 also replaces the earlier Gemma 9B bottleneck speculation with a narrower interpretation emphasizing benefits for the smaller model.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link and substantially more reproducibility information, including exact candidate weight/layer grids, GPT-2 filtering thresholds, and synthetic validation-data construction. v1's word-steering grid search was only loosely specified. One inconsistency remains in v2: Appendix E specifies Phi-3 inclusion layer 24, whereas Figure 18 labels layer 26.

R1.justification: v2 adds Prakash et al. (2024) to motivate cross-model transfer through preserved mechanisms and Radford et al. (2019) for GPT-2 quality screening. The overall research positioning remains stable; most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include local rewrites in Section 7, consolidated layer/weight-selection discussion, topical subdivision of additional appendix results, revised terminology, and the conference-publication header.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual material: multi-panel quality and accuracy breakdowns, t-SNE plots, parameter-selection and trade-off plots, and Table 13. The earlier residual-similarity and verbosity figures are retained as Figures 13 and 17a; Figure 17 gains exact-length panels. These additions substantially expand the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v1 acknowledges degenerate outputs but selects steering settings primarily through instruction accuracy. v2 addresses this important weakness with quality-screened selection and diagnostic evidence about its behavior and accuracy–quality trade-offs. More explicit search details, code/data access information, and narrower transfer claims substantially strengthen reproducibility and the credibility of practical steering claims. Quality degradation remains possible, and the Appendix E/Figure 18 layer mismatch limits reproducibility, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the gains.
